{{Short description|German mathematician (born 1971)}}
[[File:Stefanie Petermichl Oberwolfach 2025.jpg|thumb|Petermichl at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2025]]
'''Stefanie Petermichl''' (born 1971) is a German [[mathematical analysis|mathematical analyst]] who works as a professor at the [[University of Toulouse]], in France.<ref name="cv">[https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~petermic/short_vita.html Short vita], retrieved 4 July 2016.</ref> Topics of her research include [[harmonic analysis]], [[several complex variables]], [[stochastic control]], and [[elliptic partial differential equation]]s.

==Education and career==
Petermichl studied at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology]],<ref name="cv"/> and then did her graduate studies at [[Michigan State University]], completing her Ph.D. in 2000 under the supervision of [[Alexander Volberg]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=112095}}</ref> After postdoctoral studies at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] and [[Brown University]], she joined the faculty of the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 2005. She moved to the [[University of Bordeaux]] in 2007, and again to Toulouse in 2009.<ref name="cv"/> Since 2019, she holds the Humboldt chair at the [[University of Würzburg]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Petermichl Stefanie, Prof. Dr. - Institut für Mathematik |url=https://www.mathematik.uni-wuerzburg.de/harmonicanalysis/team/petermichl-stefanie/ |website=University of Würzburg |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Petermichl won the [[Salem Prize]] for 2006 "for her work on several crucial impacts to the theory of vector valued singular operators".<ref>{{citation|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|page=757|date=June–July 2007|department=Mathematics People|title=Avila and Petermichl Awarded Salem Prize|first=Jean|last=Bourgain|author-link=Jean Bourgain|volume=54|issue=6|url=http://www.ams.org/notices/200706/tx070600755p.pdf}}.</ref> She was the first woman to win that prize.<ref name="agnesscott2">{{cite web|url=http://www.agnesscott.edu/lriddle/women/prizes.htm|title=Prizes, Awards, and Honors for Women Mathematicians|publisher=agnesscott.edu|access-date=25 January 2014}}</ref> In 2012, the [[French Academy of Sciences]] gave her their Ernest Déchelle Prize.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/laureat_dechelle_math.pdf|publisher=[[French Academy of Sciences]]|title=Prix Ernest Déchelle (mathématique), lauréat de l'année 2012: Petermichl Stefanie|access-date=4 July 2016}}.</ref> She became a member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] in 2013.<ref>[http://www.iufrance.fr/les-membres-de-liuf/membre/1337-stefanie-petermichl.html Member profile], [[Institut Universitaire de France]], retrieved 4 July 2016.</ref> She is an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], speaking in the section on Analysis and Operator Algebras.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/icm-speakers|title=Speakers|work=ICM 2018|access-date=24 February 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215001530/http://www.icm2018.org/portal/en/icm-speakers|archive-date=15 December 2017}}</ref> In 2016, she was awarded a [[European Research Council]] (ERC) grant.<ref name="erc-grant">{{cite web |title=Commutators, Hilbert and Riesz transforms, Shifts, Harmonic extensions and Martingales |url=https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/682402 |website=CORDIS, European Commission |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>
